newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - Tosco soars as it joins refinery big league.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Tosco soars as it joins refinery big league.

text.p: Tosco Corp joined the ranks of the 'big league' in U.S. refining Monday with its purchase of Unocal Corp's 76 Products Co and Wall Street cheered the deal, propelling Tosco shares up more than 20 percent to an all-time high.

Tosco agreed to buy for $1.4 billion the fixed assets of 76 Products, including three refineries in California and 1,350 retail sites in the West Coast and Hawaii. With other considerations, the companies said the deal could be worth about $2 billion to Unocal, though Unocal said it would book a $375 million loss on the transaction.

Unocal will use the money to pay down enough debt to bring its debt-to-equity ratio to around 40-44 percent from 49 percent and early the company an A-rating with debt agencies, according to the company's chairman and chief executive Roger Beach.

According to Salomon Brothers analyst Paul Ting, the three additional California plants will give the acquisitive Connecticut-based Tosco a throughput of just under a million barrels of crude oil a day, or about the same in the U.S. as Amoco Corp, Exxon Corp and Mobil Corp, the nation's largest refiners.
Tosco's shares soared from Friday's close of $60-1/8 to end at a record-high $72-1/2, having been as high as $74 during the session.

"Tosco is still buying assets at the bottom of the asset cycle," said Ting. "I don't think they picked (76 Products) up for a song, as with some other Tosco purchases, but they got premium assets...and it is very accretive for shareholders," he added.

Tosco chairman and chief executive Thomas O'Malley said the deal secures the company's position as the Number One independent refiner and marketer in the country with retail fuel sales of 12 million gallons a day. O'Malley also indicated that the combination of the two companies will result in significant synergies for the main refining and retailing businesses, as well as generating substantial selling, general, and administrative cost savings.

The deal comes at a time when consolidation in the U.S. refining industry is picking up pace. Shell Oil Co and Texaco Inc said in early October that they were in talks to combine their U.S. downstream assets in the largest industry merger of its kind.

In the last couple of months, Sun Oil Co said it might close a major unit in Philadelphia and BP America Inc have said it couldn't find a buyer for an Ohio plant and will close it over the next two year.

While many in the industry have struggled to make money from refining, Tosco's O'Malley, a former Wall Street banker, has and earned a return on assets for shareholders significantly above the industry average at around 12 percent.

"You look at the returns these guys (refiners) are getting and they have to do something. But they'll tell you that the returns on marginal costs are pretty good," said Holly Gustafson, an analyst at NatWest Securities in Baltimore. In other words, the returns depend on how much you pay for the assets and Tosco has been able to buy pretty cheap.

"From Tosco's point of view we see some very interesting upside possibilities," said Ting of Salomon. "The amount of positive contribution will not be measured in nickles and dimes per share but will be much, much more significant than thatm."

Tosco will have a total of four refineries in California and one in Washington state after the deal. It also has plants in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. O'Malley said Monday that the 76 Products plants complement each other, though some analysts said closure of one of more of the California sites is possible, and a big reduction of headcount likely in any case.
Tosco is expected to say more about its plans for the plants in briefings on Tuesday, analysts said.
Unocal, which said just three weeks ago that it was considering selling the 76 Products unit, was also seen benefitting out of the deal.

"They got a good value out of this," said Anit Sen, who follows Unocal for Wall Street brokerage Oppenheimer & Co. The deal also allows Unocal to save $200 million to $250 million in capital expenditures on California downstream which it will redirect to the international exploration and production side, Sen said.
It plans to use $800 million from its sale to pay down debt and will also consider a stock repurchase plan, Unocal's Beach said, at a conference call.

As part of the deal, Unocal can receive additional payments from Tosco of up to $250 million over seven years if California marketing margins improve, though analysts noted that this is a very large unknown.
"If margins stay flat, we would not get anything," Beach said. "It's just an upside sharing" agreement.
"I wonder if they (Unocal) might not have done better from an aggregate shareholder standpoint from a tax-free spin-off," said Mark Gilman, an analyst at UBS Securities.

"The most interesting question for Unocal is what the market is going to say about it from a valuation point of view," Gilman added. Unocal's shares were up from Friday's close of $39-1/2 at $40-1/2, though Gilman said he was sticking with his valuation for the company of just $31 to $32 a share.
